source_section: Definition, One variable: nonzero polynomial over commutative ring with 1
mathematical_source_observation: For a nonzero polynomial P=∑_{k=0}^n a_k X^k in R[X] over a commutative unital ring R, deg(P) is the greatest exponent k whose coefficient a_k≠0_R. Equivalently, for a canonical finite-support coefficient sequence a_k, it is the maximum support index.
scope_and_caveat: Requires a nonzero formal polynomial, ring with unity and a distinguished indeterminate. Do not treat arbitrary polynomial functions as equal to the formal ring element, especially over finite fields or rings with zero divisors. Do not identify zero polynomial degree with 0; common algebraic convention sets deg(0)=−∞, but the selected source leaves it undefined. The ProofWiki composite page includes a misleading 'Degree Zero' subheading and a field subpage flagged for refactoring; independently cross-check the principal nonzero coefficient criterion.
candidate_formulations: nonzero formal polynomial highest nonzero coefficient index
finite-support coefficient sequence maximum support index
zero polynomial degree convention as a separate unscreened variant

source_section: Proper Riemann integrability via epsilon-delta over every tagged finite partition
mathematical_source_observation: For a bounded real-valued f on a compact interval [a,b], let P range over partitions a=x_0<…<x_n=b with tagged samples ξ_i∈[x_{i-1},x_i]. Define S(f;P,ξ)=Σ f(ξ_i)(x_i−x_{i-1}) and mesh(P)=max_i(x_i−x_{i-1}). Proper Riemann integrability means there exists L∈R such that for every ε>0 there exists δ>0 and for every tagged partition with mesh<δ the sum differs from L by <ε.
scope_and_caveat: Stronger universal quantified tagged partition definition on bounded closed intervals. The OpenStax §5.2 equal-width Riemann-sum presentation is pedagogical and not safely equivalent for arbitrary bounded f without hypotheses; do not substitute a single prescribed sequence of sums for the all-tags/all-refinements criterion. Improper integrals on infinite/open intervals, Lebesgue integrals and Lebesgue–Stieltjes integrals require separate source contexts.
candidate_formulations: proper Riemann integral over bounded interval all tagged partitions
OpenStax equal-partition calculus exposition, not assumed equivalent without additional hypotheses
improper interval integration separate future context

source_section: §18.2(ix), Equation 18.2.26, moments of an orthogonality measure
mathematical_source_observation: Given a positive orthogonality measure μ on a real interval and a nonnegative integer n for which the integral exists, the n-th (raw) moment is μ_n = ∫_a^b x^n dμ(x). In the orthogonal polynomial chapter the measure is assumed to have all the required finite moments.
scope_and_caveat: The DLMF raw moment definition depends on an independently understood positive measure and Stieltjes/Lebesgue–Stieltjes integration; a moment is not the same mathematical object as μ itself, and finite moments are additional hypotheses, not automatically true of all measures. Distinguish central moments from raw moments and probability-normalized measures from general nonnegative finite measures.
candidate_formulations: nth raw moment of an orthogonality measure
finite all-moments condition as separate property
